newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends week down in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends week down in thin trade.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended another week lower as the market remained starved of demand and lacked positive leads from other trading centres in the region, traders said.
They said no inquiries were received from potential buyers and trading was sluggish throughout the day.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted June RSS1 buyer at 269.50 cents ($1.08) a kg, down two cents from Wednesday. June SMR20 buyer was one cent lower at 255. The Malaysian rubber market was closed on Thursday for a religious holiday.
Trading houses were offering the SMR20 at 253 cents, SMR CV at 327, SMR L at 305, SMR 5 at 265, SMR10 at 254 and latex at 225.
Traders said official prices of the RSS1 fell 6.5 cents and the SMR20 4.5 cents through the week.
The INRO five-day indicator was, however, higher at 207.91 on May 8 from the 207.84 on May 7. The daily indicator was at 207.77, compared to 207.12 a day earlier.
